newsitem.title: USA: October housing starts rate lowest in a year.
newsitem.headline: October housing starts rate lowest in a year.

text.p: Builders broke ground on new homes and apartments at the slowest rate in a year during October, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as the housing industry steadily lost steam.
Total starts fell 5.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.366 million -- the lowest rate since 1.351 million in October 1995 -- after a revised 6.1 percent drop in October.
Applications for building permits declined for a third consecutive month, suggesting the pace of building will continue to wind down in coming months.
The building rate for single-family homes of 1.069 million a year during October was the lowest since June 1995, when it was at 1.036 million.
The building industry enjoyed an exceptionally strong first half, but a weakening trend set in during the summer.
The slower October building pace was the latest indication that a slowdown in national economic activity, which became apparent during the third quarter, was continuing.
Previously, the department said September building starts had fallen 6 percent, but it revised that to show a slightly steeper drop of 6.1 percent.

The National Association of Home Builders said on Monday that its index of market activity dropped four points in November to 51 from 55 in October as sales and visitor traffic to model sites eased off.
"The very strong level of housing activity achieved in the first half of the year simply could not be sustained," said assocation president Randy Smith, a builder in Walnut Creek, Calif.

The decline in building activity during October was widespread. Not only did single-family starts decline, but starts on apartments also dropped 7.2 percent to a rate of 297,000 following an 8.8 percent increase in September.

The falloff in October building occurred despite cheaper mortgages in October. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.85 percent in October, down from 8.03 percent in September.
Regionally, starts fell everywhere except in the West, where they increased 6.5 percent to a rate of 358,000 a year.
In the Northeast they decreased 9.3 percent to 127,000 a year and in the Midwest they were down 9.2 percent to a rate of 277,000. In the South starts fell 8.3 percent to 604,000 a year.
Applications for new building permits dropped 2.7 percent last month to a rate of 1.361 million a year, the lowest since 1.358 million in July last year.
